items.title: #775 - From Failed Products to Amazon Bestsellers
items.excerpt: Two friends hit $2M in their first year on Amazon. Hear how failed products, smarter sourcing, and ideas inspired by problems helped them build brands and find their next growth opportunity.
items.body: Two friends hit $2M in their first year on Amazon. Hear how failed products, smarter sourcing, and ideas inspired by problems helped them build brands and find their next growth opportunity. ► Watch The Podcasts On Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/@Helium10?sub_confirmation=1 ► Instagram: instagram.com/serioussellerspodcast ► Free Amazon Seller Chrome Extension: https://h10.me/extension ► Sign Up For Helium 10: https://h10.me/signup (Use SSP10 To Save 10% For Life) ► Learn How To Sell on Amazon: https://h10.me/ft What starts as an attempt to cover a cash flow gap can become something much bigger. In this episode of the Serious Sellers Podcast, Bradley Sutton meets longtime friends and business partners Daniel Gray and Kristian Ball in Chester, England. When rising energy costs squeezed their digital billboard business, they turned to Amazon to generate additional income. Their early success reselling payment terminals helped open the door, but repeated intellectual property issues pushed them toward building their own brands. They report reaching $2 million in turnover during their first year on Amazon. Their private label journey came with expensive lessons. A hair powder product struggled against established competitors, while a slug trap enjoyed strong initial sales before demand weakened in subsequent years. Their sports training brand, Skillbox, grew from a problem they understood firsthand: keeping their children engaged in football practice. By turning training exercises into a dice game, they created a product that sold out within two weeks of its Christmas launch. Their nasal strip product followed a similar approach, addressing Kristian’s frustration with strips that would not stay on during exercise. items.title: 请帮忙分析下shein女装还能用自运营的模式么？只有10万本金和2人团队，想做小而美且稳，不做大做强。
items.excerpt: 自己做亚马逊多年到了瓶颈期，现在有做shein的机会（只做美区）。 优势：合伙人为服装设计师，曾开发过shein多个爆款，有供应链资源，能hold住设计打板样衣到生产所有环节。 劣势：本金只有10W左右，团队就2个人，没有独立工厂。 全托管不考虑，担心没有足够的资金量来应对可能的爆款。 自运营是优选，但是账号是个大难题，现在买来的账号还靠谱么？ 半托不是很懂，能自主控制发货量，且有一点点定价权力么？ 想做小而美且稳，不做大做强。

items.body: Why does this $3.5M Amazon seller spend more on Sponsored Brands than Sponsored Products? In this episode of the Serious Sellers Podcast, Bradley Sutton meets returning guest Amina Salakhova at Swords Castle in Dublin, Ireland, to explore how she and her husband have done exactly that. With approximately $3.5 million in sales and their sights set on $4 million, Amina shares how expanding across Europe has helped their business thrive. Germany leads their sales, followed by France and Italy, while smaller marketplaces such as Belgium and Ireland offer opportunities to establish a presence early. Her approach to localization goes beyond translation, combining keyword research from Helium 10’s Cerebro and Magnet with ChatGPT to create listings around the terms local shoppers actually use. Competing in a crowded category also means giving customers a reason to choose your product. Amina explains how premium screen protectors, thoughtful packaging, installation kits, and clear instructions help justify higher prices and encourage repeat purchases.
